title: Compatible first-page continuity and abutment quotient models
statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category, D:I→Scheme a diagram of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions and limit cone c. Let F_i be complexes of abelian etale sheaves with compatible unital inverse-image transitions and F_i^n=0 for n<a, using the canonical composition isomorphisms. Let G:I^op→CochainComplex on c.pt be the inverse-image diagram with its compatible isomorphisms eG, and L its colimit cocone. Fix p in Z. Let P be canonical degree-p derived pullback (specified by the derived adjunction unit), H:I^op→AddCommGrpCat the degree-p stage hypercohomology diagram via compatible isomorphisms eH, and B a cocone on H with an isomorphism eB to the degree-p hypercohomology of L.pt intertwining its legs with P and the colimit complex maps. Set $N=\max(p+1-a,0)$. There exist a nonempty directed preorder $J$ of universe $u+1$, a stage-selection function $k:J\to I$, a functor $E:J\to\operatorname{SpectralSequence}(\mathrm{Ab})$ starting on page one, a target spectral sequence $E^\prime$, compatible spectral maps $v_j:E_j\to E^\prime$, and additive subgroups $S_n\subseteq B$, with $S_0=B$, $S_N=0$, and $S$ antitone. The differential shape is $(t,s)\mapsto(t+1-r,s+r)$ at page $r$. At each bidegree, every map from the colimit of the first-page terms to the target first-page term satisfying the equations induced by $v$ is an isomorphism. For every $n<N$, there are a common finite page $r\ge1$, subgroups $T_j\subseteq H(k(j))$, and homomorphisms $q:S_n\to (E^\prime_r)^{p-a-n,a+n}$ and $t_j:T_j\to E_{r,j}^{p-a-n,a+n}$ such that $q(x)=0$ if and only if $x\in S_{n+1}$, each $t_j$ is surjective, and for every $y\in T_j$ the image $B_{k(j)}(y)$ belongs to $S_n$ and $q(B_{k(j)}(y))=v_{r,j}(t_j(y))$. No comparison isomorphism is asserted on the later pages. Spectral sequences are as in [def-sp-spectral-sequence]; the directed indexing and colimits are those of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: Apply directed cofinal reindexing to the filtered opposite of I with index A in universe u. Whisker the scheme cone and complex cocone with this same reindexing. Degreewise evaluation computes the colimit of complexes. Exact inverse image and termwise colimits preserve the common lower bound a. Perform sheaf continuity on A before setting J=ULift A in universe u+1; the equivalence J≃A transports diagrams and their colimit cocones. Its selected original stages define k.

Choose the functorial termwise hypercohomology presentations and maps for the stage transitions and limit legs. The specified identity and composition equations on φ and G and the corresponding laws for the spectral maps assemble E and the compatible v. Swap coordinates so that page-r differentials have bidegree (1-r,r). The resolution/derived-global-sections comparison fixes the abutment identifications.

On the small directed index A in universe u, for every nonnegative resolution degree and every complex degree apply sheaf cohomology continuity to the corresponding term. The first-page identifications and their pullback naturality identify these colimit maps with those induced by v. Negative resolution degrees have zero groups at every stage and at the target. Transport the resulting first-page colimit cocone along the equivalence J≃A. In either case the page-one cocone on J is a colimit, so each ψ with its displayed equations is the canonical isomorphism. This avoids applying the continuity theorem to an index of universe u+1 while keeping schemes of universe u.

The first page is supported in resolution degree t≥0 and complex degree s≥a. The next page is homology, so vanishing off this region persists. At (t,s), the outgoing differential has target (t+1-r,s+r) and the incoming source is (t+r-1,s-r). Both are zero for r>max(t+1,s-a), uniformly over stages and target. The canonical subquotient convergence descriptions identify this common stationary page with the abutment graded pieces, compatibly with v. This uses no assertion that the page-r comparison is an isomorphism.

Transport the degree-p target abutment filtration along eB and put S_n at a+n. The support implies the whole bound at a and zero bound at p+1. For p<a the abutment is zero and N=0, giving both bounds at the same step. Otherwise use N=(p+1-a).toNat and antitonicity. At each n<N, let T_j be the stage step a+n, pulled back along eH. The quotient projections followed by the inverse common-page convergence isomorphisms define q and t_j. Quotient exactness gives ker(q)=S_(n+1) and surjectivity of every t_j. Filtered pullback functoriality preserves the steps and commutes with the quotient projections. Its abutment clause, hP, hH and hB identify the underlying stage-to-limit map with B_j, proving the last equation. This step does not lift a target page class from any stage.
